outline: 172 Inequalities with Variables in the Denominator

examples.solution_text:
For $x<2$:
$\begin{align*}2-x&<x+2\\-2x&<0\\x&>0\end{align*}$
Within this case, $0<x<2$.
For $x\ge2$, $x-2<x+2$ always holds.
Combining the valid intervals gives $(0,\infty)$.

examples.question_text: Sketch $y=|x-4|$ and $y=x+2$ on the same axes, hence solve $|x-4|<x+2$.
Sketch $y=|x-3|$ and $y=|x+1|$ on the same axes, hence solve $|x-3|\le|x+1|$.

examples.solution_text:
The sign boundaries are $x=-\frac12$ and $x=5$.
For $x<-\frac12$:
$\begin{align*}-2x-1&\le5-x\\-x&\le6\\x&\ge-6\end{align*}$
Within this case, $-6\le x<-\frac12$.
For $-\frac12\le x<5$:
$\begin{align*}2x+1&\le5-x\\3x&\le4\\x&\le\frac43\end{align*}$
Within this case, $-\frac12\le x\le\frac43$.
For $x\ge5$:
$\begin{align*}2x+1&\le x-5\\x&\le-6\end{align*}$
This contradicts $x\ge5$.
Combining the valid intervals gives $[-6,\frac43]$.

The right side must be positive, so $x>-6$.
The absolute-value inequality requires both $-(x+6)<x-4$ and $x-4<x+6$.
$\begin{align*}-x-6&<x-4\\-2&<2x\\x&>-1\end{align*}$
The other inequality, $x-4<x+6$, holds for every real $x$.
Combining these conditions gives $(-1,\infty)$.

The denominator excludes $x=6$. For $x\ne6$, $8|x-6|$ is positive, so multiplication preserves the inequality:
$x|x-6|\ge8$.
For $x>6$:
$\begin{align*}x(x-6)&\ge8\\x^2-6x-8&\ge0\end{align*}$
The boundary values are $3-\sqrt{17}$ and $3+\sqrt{17}$. The quadratic is nonnegative outside these values. Within $x>6$, this gives $x\ge3+\sqrt{17}$.
For $x<6$:
$\begin{align*}x(6-x)&\ge8\\x^2-6x+8&\le0\\(x-2)(x-4)&\le0\end{align*}$
Thus $2\le x\le4$, which lies within this case.
Combining the valid intervals gives $[2,4]\cup[3+\sqrt{17},\infty)$. The excluded value $x=6$ is in neither interval.

examples.derivation: For x<2, 2-x<x+2 gives x>0, hence 0<x<2. For x≥2, x-2<x+2 always holds. The union is (0,∞). The plotted vertex (2,0), line intercept (0,2) and intersection (0,2) agree with the functions. Formatting preserves the original mathematics, ticks, plotted domain and method.

The left branch satisfies 4-x=x+2 at x=1, y=3. The right branch x-4 is always below x+2. The absolute-value graph is below the line exactly for x>1, giving (1,∞). Both plotted functions and the solution-only intersection annotation agree.

Between vertices -1 and 3, equality is 3-x=x+1, giving (1,2). Left of -1 the first graph is 4 units higher; right of 3 it is 4 units lower. Between the vertices, the first graph is no higher exactly when x≥1. Thus [1,∞), consistent with the plotted vertices, branches and annotation.

For x<-1/2, -2x-1≤5-x gives x≥-6, retaining [-6,-1/2). For -1/2≤x<5, 2x+1≤5-x gives x≤4/3, retaining [-1/2,4/3]. For x≥5, 2x+1≤x-5 requires x≤-6 and contributes nothing. The union is [-6,4/3]. No diagram is required for this cases solution.

Require x+6>0. The lower bound -x-6<x-4 gives -2<2x, hence x>-1. The upper bound x-4<x+6 always holds. Intersecting with x>-6 gives (-1,∞). This uses the booklet's simultaneous absolute-value bounds; no diagram is required.

Exclude x=6 and multiply by positive 8|x-6| to obtain x|x-6|≥8. For x>6, x²-6x-8≥0 has roots 3±√17; the case retains x≥3+√17. For x<6, x(6-x)≥8 becomes (x-2)(x-4)≤0, retaining [2,4]. The union is [2,4]∪[3+√17,∞), which excludes 6. No diagram is required for the requested cases method.
